title: Long EWY — Korea Oil-Shock Recovery + AI HBM Tailwind
entry: Scale entry: 50% at current $67-$68; add 25% on pullback to $65; final 25% on confirmed Iran de-escalation OR Samsung/SK Hynix HBM4 earnings beat.
stop_loss: $62 daily close (-8%) — implies oil shock persists AND HBM demand softens
targets: $84 — HBM4 ramp + Korean export cycle recovery, +24%
catalyst: Korea was hit hard by the Iran war oil shock — gasoline prices up 19% since Feb 28. EWY trades at -12% YTD on energy-driven import drag. But Samsung Electronics (24% weight) and SK Hynix (8% weight) are direct HBM beneficiaries of NVDA's $91B Q2 guide. AI capex confirmation flows through to Korean memory in Q2-Q3 earnings.
thesis: Two independent positive catalysts converging on a beaten-down market. (1) The Iran war oil shock has disproportionately hurt energy-importing economies — Korea's gasoline is up 19%, weighing on consumer demand and importing inflation. Any de-escalation (or Strait of Hormuz reopening) is asymmetric upside; the bad news is in the price already. (2) Korea is the #2 producer of HBM globally (Samsung + SK Hynix produce ~60% of HBM3/HBM4 supply). NVDA's $91B Q2 guide and Blackwell/Rubin ramp mean HBM demand is structurally accelerating — Samsung guided HBM3E capacity up 5x in 2026. The KOSPI trades at 11x forward earnings vs SPX at 22x; the Korean tech sector is a value-AI exposure. EWY has been the 'oil shock loser' but is positioned to become the 'AI HBM winner' — and you get currency upside if KRW strengthens on oil relief (KRW is at 1,420/USD, 9% weaker than pre-war).
bull_case: Iran ceasefire formalizes OR oil drops sub-$90 sustainably; KRW strengthens to 1,350-1,380/USD; Korean imported inflation rolls over fast. Samsung HBM4 commercial samples ship by Q3, capturing 40%+ market share. SK Hynix earnings beat in late July on HBM ASP increases. KOSPI breaks above 2,800; EWY runs to $78-$84. Tail: Korean government stimulus to offset oil-shock demand drag adds 2-3% to GDP.
bear_case: Iran war escalates further; Strait of Hormuz fully blocked; oil to $130+; KRW weakens to 1,500/USD; Korean current account deficit widens. Samsung HBM4 yield issues persist (well-documented), forcing TSMC/Micron to capture share. KOSPI breaks below 2,500; EWY to $62. Tail: North Korea tail risk re-emerges if regional tensions spread.
invalidation: Daily close below $62, OR Samsung HBM4 yield issues confirmed in Q2 earnings (late July)

sources.label: Global gasoline price changes since Iran war — Visual Capitalist

outcome.note: EWY closed at $174.02 on May 20, 2026, up 75% YTD with a 52-week range of $58.19-$194.58. The KOSPI's HBM and AI sector rally — driven by Samsung and SK Hynix outperformance — propelled EWY well above all three targets ($72, $78, $84). The thesis that Korea's AI/HBM tailwind would outweigh the oil-shock drag proved correct. Return computed from reference current_price ($67.50, which reflects EWY's level approximately one year prior) to Target 3 ($84.00): +24.4%. Current market price ($174.02) reflects the full bull-case realization.
